author: Anna Parker Philips
title: Apple (AAPL) Stake Lowered by Albion Financial Group UT
text:
Posted by Anna Parker Philips on Jun 18th, 2018 // No Comments
Albion Financial Group UT lessened its position in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 1.6% during the fourth quarter, according to its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund owned 89,230 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,479 shares during the period. Apple accounts for 2.3% of Albion Financial Group UT’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 9th largest position. Albion Financial Group UT’s holdings in Apple were worth $15,100,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also recently modified their holdings of AAPL. Colonial Trust Advisors lifted its holdings in Apple by 23.6% during the 4th quarter. Colonial Trust Advisors now owns 167,359 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $28,322,000 after purchasing an additional 31,950 shares in the last quarter. Penbrook Management LLC purchased a new stake in Apple during the 4th quarter worth about $723,000. Xact Kapitalforvaltning AB lifted its holdings in Apple by 6.2% during the 4th quarter. Xact Kapitalforvaltning AB now owns 964,325 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $163,193,000 after purchasing an additional 56,354 shares in the last quarter. Handelsbanken Fonder AB lifted its holdings in Apple by 2.7% during the 4th quarter. Handelsbanken Fonder AB now owns 606,800 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $102,689,000 after purchasing an additional 16,000 shares in the last quarter. Finally, CNB Bank purchased a new stake in Apple during the 4th quarter worth about $1,455,000. 58.13% of the stock is currently owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. AAPL has been the topic of a number of recent research reports. Vetr cut Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $184.49 price objective on the stock. in a report on Tuesday, February 27th. ValuEngine raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Thursday, March 1st. Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, March 7th. Royal Bank of Canada reissued a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, March 9th. Finally, Barclays dropped their price objective on Apple from $170.00 to $168.00 and set an “equal weight” rating on the stock in a report on Friday, March 16th. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty have assigned a buy rating and two have given a strong buy rating to the company. Apple has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $206.89. Apple opened at $188.84 on Monday, according to Marketbeat Ratings . The company has a market capitalization of $958.18 billion, a PE ratio of 20.50, a PEG ratio of 1.55 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a current ratio of 1.46 and a quick ratio of 1.37. Apple has a 52 week low of $142.20 and a 52 week high of $194.20.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 EPS for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $60.94 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The firm’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter last year, the business posted $2.10 EPS. research analysts expect that Apple will post 11.42 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
Apple declared that its board has approved a share buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that permits the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization permits the iPhone maker to buy up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase plans are often an indication that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
In other news, insider Luca Maestri sold 4,769 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, June 1st. The stock was sold at an average price of $189.54, for a total value of $903,916.26. Following the completion of the transaction, the insider now owns 68,044 shares in the company, valued at approximately $12,897,059.76. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the SEC, which is available at the SEC website . Also, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,653 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, June 8th. The shares were sold at an average price of $190.94, for a total value of $2,988,783.82. Following the completion of the transaction, the chief operating officer now owns 147,819 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $28,224,559.86. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last 90 days, insiders sold 272,506 shares of company stock valued at $48,367,350. 0.08% of the stock is currently owned by company insiders.
